discovery: Theory of topological superconductivity and Majorana bound states
motivation: Read (with Green, 2000) showed that chiral p-wave superconductors are topological phases whose vortices and edges host Majorana zero modes with non-Abelian statistics. Kitaev's one-dimensional chain (2001) gave the minimal model of unpaired Majorana end states and connected them to fault-tolerant topological quantum computation. Fu (with Kane, 2008) showed that ordinary s-wave superconductors proximitized onto topological-insulator surfaces realize this physics, which opened the route to engineered hybrid devices. Together these works turned surface Andreev bound states into a unifying principle. Bulk topology fixes protected boundary modes, and the same principle explains zero-bias conductance anomalies, fractional Josephson effects and odd-frequency pairing. Their ideas define the classification of topological superconductors and drive an extensive worldwide program of experiments in nanowires, vortex cores, iron-based and hybrid junctions. The framework is a lasting conceptual advance in quantum matter.
